Required probability \(= 1 - \frac{1}{145} = \frac{144}{145}\).

December has 31 days, that is 4 full weeks and 3 extra days. The 4 weeks give 4 Sundays.

There is a 5th Sunday only if one of the 3 extra days (December 1, 2 or 3) is a Sunday. December 1 can fall on any of the 7 days of the week, and 3 of these give 5 Sundays.

Required probability \(= \frac{3}{7}\).

The differences between terms are 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, ..., an A.P. with first term 4 and common difference 2.

So \(T_{n} = 3 + [4 + 6 + \cdots \text{ to } (n - 1) \text{ terms}] = 3 + \frac{n - 1}{2}\,[2(4) + (n - 2)(2)] = 3 + (n - 1)(n + 2)\).

text: The second derivative of \(a\sin^{3}t\) with respect to \(a\cos^{3}t\) at \(t = \frac{\pi}{4}\) is
solution:
Let \(y = a\sin^{3}t\) and \(x = a\cos^{3}t\). Then

\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3a\sin^{2}t\cos t}{-3a\cos^{2}t\sin t} = -\tan t\).

Differentiating again with respect to x:

\(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = -\sec^{2}t\,\frac{dt}{dx} = \frac{-\sec^{2}t}{-3a\cos^{2}t\sin t} = \frac{\sec^{4}t}{3a\sin t}\).

At \(t = \frac{\pi}{4}\): \(\sec^{4}t = 4\) and \(\sin t = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3a}\).
